title: Pro-etale localization preserves injectives
statement:
For a weakly etale $v:W\to X$, the site $W_{\Proet}$ is the slice of
$X_{\Proet}$ over $W$. The restriction functor on constant-coefficient module
sheaves is exact and preserves injectives. Consequently derived evaluation on
$W$, computed in sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$, agrees with derived global sections
on $W_{\Proet}$.

proof.text: Work with the universes and bounded small-site objects of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Composition of weakly etale maps is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]; [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects] supplies the additional permanence assertion, which the former node does not state. Send an object $V\to W$ to $(V\to X,V\to W)$ in $X_{\Proet}/W$. Composition makes it an object of $X_{\Proet}$. Conversely, for a slice object $(V\to X,s:V\to W)$, permanence makes $s$ weakly etale. These assignments are inverse on objects and on the scheme morphisms commuting with the structural maps. A covering on either side is the same family of underlying weakly etale morphisms of schemes, with the same finite-affine fpqc condition in the site definition, so the assignments identify coverings as well. In particular $\mathrm{id}_W$ is the final slice object. The size bounds are those of the common site convention, so the identification is between the chosen sites, up to the harmless choice of skeleton.

Let $\Lambda$ be the constant coefficient ring. In the finite-coefficient convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], restriction of the coefficient presheaf $V\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|V|),\Lambda)$ has the identical formula on $(V,s)$; sheafification on this slice uses precisely the coverings of $V$ over $W$, so its associated ring sheaf is $\Lambda_{W,\Proet}$. For an ordinary constant ring sheaf the same verification starts with the constant presheaf. Thus write $\mathcal O=\Lambda_{X,\Proet}$ and $\mathcal O|_W=\Lambda_{W,\Proet}$. Form $P_M(V)=\bigoplus_{s:V\to W\text{ over }X}M(V,s)$ with the restrictions and componentwise $\mathcal O(V)$-action of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], and put $j_!M=P_M^\#$ using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This is the slice construction; [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is only its etale special case, not an assertion about weakly etale maps. A module map $M\to j^*N$ gives the map $P_M(V)\to N(V)$ obtained by summing its component maps. Conversely a map $P_M\to N$ restricts on the summand indexed by $s$ to $M(V,s)\to N(V)$; naturality makes these a map on the slice. The two operations are inverse since a map from a direct sum is determined by its summands. Sheafification's universal property identifies module maps $P_M\to N$ with maps $j_!M\to N$. Hence $j_!\dashv j^*$, naturally in both arguments. This calculation uses only left module actions, not commutativity of $\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: direct-sum construction and adjunction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives] to the underlying abelian sheaves on the slice. It supplies an exact extension functor left adjoint to restriction, and exactness of restriction. The abelian specialization of the explicit adjunction in step 2 identifies its left adjoint with the sheafified direct-sum construction by uniqueness of left adjoints; the identification is natural, so that construction is exact as well. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise and cokernels are sheafifications of the sectionwise cokernels; forgetting the action therefore detects exactness. The construction in step 2 has exactly these underlying abelian extension and restriction functors, so $j_!$ and $j^*$ are exact for the coefficient ring $\Lambda$, including noncommutative rings. In the finite-coefficient setting the exactness of inverse image is also [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The adjunction of step 2 and exactness of $j_!$ meet precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], with $u=j_!$ and $u_*=j^*$; thus restriction preserves injective module sheaves. No assertion that an injective module sheaf remains injective after forgetting its action is used.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph exactness and third paragraph injective preservation

proof.text: For an unbounded complex $K$ on $X_{\Proet}$, take a K-injective resolution $K\to I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]; the small skeleton and coefficient universe in step 1 satisfy their small-site hypotheses, and the ring-sheaf theorem does not assume commutativity. Exactness of $j^*$ makes $j^*K\to j^*I$ a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to the additive pair $j_!\dashv j^*$ of steps 2-3: $j_!$ is exact, so $j^*I$ is K-injective on the slice. For every integer $n$, the equality $(j^*I)^n(\mathrm{id}_W)=I^n(W)$ commutes with the differentials because restriction applies to the same sheaf maps. Consequently the complexes computing $R\Gamma(W,K)$ on $X_{\Proet}$ and $R\Gamma(W_{\Proet},j^*K)$ are identical, not merely cohomologically isomorphic. The maps for a chain map $I\to I'$ are identical by the same sectionwise equality, and homotopies restrict sectionwise as well, By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived morphism between the chosen K-injective representatives is represented by a chain map uniquely up to homotopy, and quasi-isomorphisms between such representatives are homotopy equivalences. The preceding equality on chain maps and homotopies therefore descends to the canonical natural comparison on the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], independently of the chosen representatives. For commutative coefficients this is the derived-operations convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For a sheaf, or a bounded-below complex, step 3 also permits the ordinary injective-resolution computation in the blueprint; the K-injective argument supplies the unbounded case without imposing a boundedness hypothesis.
